B: Hey! Hiya, you alright? I'm Callum.
A: Hi. Adam. Yeah, not bad, you?
B: Yeah, good, good. Okay, I'm just gonna say it, I clocked the stone bookends in your photo. Are they actual stone? What's the story there?
A: Er, yeah. Offcuts. I'm a stonemason, so they're just bits from work.
B: No way. Proper stonemason? Like, carving and that?
A: Bit of carving. Mostly repair work. Old sandstone buildings round Bradford, a lot of it's listed. Half the week I'm in the workshop cutting and dressing stone, half on site fixing it in.
B: That's amazing, honestly. I'm a structural engineer, so I'm sort of the other end of it. Concrete frames, steel, new-build residential mostly in Birmingham. Which is fine, but it's not exactly Gothic Revival, you know?
A: Ha. No. Somebody's got to do it, though.
B: Somebody's got to do it. But your stuff's going to be standing in two hundred years, mine's got a design life of sixty. Do you work in lime?
A: Yeah, always lime on the old stuff. If you put cement mortar in sandstone it's harder than the stone, so the water can't get out through the joint and it comes out through the stone instead. Then the face just blows off. You see it all over Bradford, people repointing their terraces with cement in the eighties and now the fronts are sort of crumbling.
B: Oh, that makes total sense, right, you want the mortar to be the sacrificial bit.
A: Exactly that. Joint goes before the stone does. It's easier to repoint than replace a block.
B: Love that. Where's the best thing you've worked on, then?
A: Er. There was a chapel in Saltaire, some of the window tracery. Took me weeks, that, getting the templates right. I was quite chuffed with it.
B: Saltaire's brilliant. I went to Salts Mill for the Hockney stuff when I was at uni.
A: Yeah, I'm only up the road in Shipley. I've been round it more times than I can count. There's a good podcast on the history of the village, actually, how Titus Salt laid it all out.
B: Send me that. Not that we can, can we, it's all anonymous. Anyway. Have you been abroad for buildings? I'm a bit obsessed, I did Porto, Rotterdam, Japan last spring.
A: Florence. Just the once.
B: Ah, Florence.
A: I still go on about it. The Duomo, the marble, you just stand there thinking how did they set this out without any of the kit we've got. Spain and Portugal are next, northern Spain mainly.
B: Oh, do Porto, honestly, the granite there is unreal. And Santiago's not far.
A: Santiago's on the list, yeah.
B: Did you do that puzzle at the start, by the way? I got proper wound up by the last one.
A: Er, I was a bit slow on it. Ran out of time on two.
B: Same, I think it was rigged. Do you ever get engineers on your jobs, like, telling you what to do?
A: Sometimes. They're alright mostly. Some of them have never stood on a scaffold, mind.
B: Ha, fair, that's fair, that's me in a few years probably.
A: You'll be alright. You sound like you'd at least ask.
B: I ask too much, that's my problem, ask Hannah. Okay, so the tracery, did you draw the templates by hand or
